stem.text: The diagrams show the structures of two isomeric dicarboxylic acids, $X$ and $Y$.

stem.alt: Displayed structure of X: HO2C-CH=CH-CO2H drawn with C=O groups, OH groups and two H atoms on the C=C, with the two CO2H groups on the same side of the double bond.
stem.label: X

stem.alt: Displayed structure of Y: HO2C-C(H)=C(H)-CO2H drawn with C=O groups, OH groups and H atoms on the C=C, with the two CO2H groups on opposite sides of the double bond.
stem.label: Y

stem.text: $X$ can be reduced to compound $P$ with empirical formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}$.
$Y$ can be reduced to compound $Q$, also with empirical formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}$.

A.text: $X$ is a cis isomer; compound $P$ and compound $Q$ are identical.

B.text: $X$ is a cis isomer; compound $P$ and compound $Q$ are isomers of each other.

C.text: $X$ is a trans isomer; compound $P$ and compound $Q$ are identical.

D.text: $X$ is a trans isomer; compound $P$ and compound $Q$ are isomers of each other.
